htgr.summary: Generic helium-cooled reactor that supplies all process heat through the IHX, with a branch to the power block.
lims: The design basis is a generic 925°C HTGR. No commercial reactor runs at this outlet, and Xe-100 is only a labelled analogue with a much lower outlet temperature.
The decay heat limit at this rating and outlet temperature is unchecked.
Heat beyond the process need is held as margin and earns no revenue.
The anchored port reports heat shortfall as grid import and has no unmet thermal demand field.
Input outside its evidence range. Helium supply temperature is fixed at 900 C. Highest measured secondary helium temperature is 859 C, HTTR 2004 high-temperature run (IAEA NP-T-4.3 printed p.14)

circ_primary.summary: Helium circulators. Figure 2 draws the primary circulator; the engine counts the secondary circulator on the return leg as well.
lims: No measured circulator shaft power exists in the local sources.
Whether INL's power conversion efficiency is already net of primary circulation is unverified, so this load may be counted twice.
The secondary loop pressure drop is an assumption. INL's per-exchanger labels imply a larger drop, which would raise the circulator load.
The secondary circulator inlet sits above the circulator inlet temperatures run at HTTR.

ihx.summary: Helium to helium exchanger between the primary loop and the secondary loop that heats the reformer.
lims: The approach is a modelling assumption below every measured IHX approach in the local sources; the engine flag below gives the evidence range.
No IHX in the local sources has run at this secondary helium temperature.
The required conductance of a single unit is far above HTTR's, so the module count is open.
The anchored port has no IHX duty field; it computes only the loss terms around the IHX.
Input outside its evidence range. IHX approach at 25 K lies outside the evidence range 50 to 82 K, and the cross rules cap the control at 50 K
Input outside its evidence range. Helium supply temperature is fixed at 900 C. Highest measured secondary helium temperature is 859 C, HTTR 2004 high-temperature run (IAEA NP-T-4.3 printed p.14)

power.summary: Small steam plant on a primary helium branch. It raises electricity for site loads and steam for the reboiler gap.
lims: The efficiency traces to TEV-981, which is not held locally, so whether it is net of circulation is unknown.
The block is a small steam plant with process extraction, sized by this balance with no equipment design.
Unmet electrical demand is reported as grid import at rating.

smr.summary: Reformer tubes heated by secondary helium in place of fired furnaces.
lims: Stage 2 tube check. On the assumed tube (Hoseinzade and Adams geometry with the JAERI finned helium annulus) and helium supplied at 900°C, the tube model found no tube count in its search range that reaches the 871°C exit. The two lower exit temperatures of the Stage 2 sensitivity, flowsheet runs FS_B_REC_F_T825 and FS_B_REC_F_T800, are reachable. The design exit therefore stays INL's equilibrium assumption, and the Headline solve does not use the tube model.
Stage 2 JAERI benchmark. The A-2 run sets the single tuned catalyst activity, and the held-back runs miss the measured methane conversion.
The Xu and Froment rates are extrapolated well above the temperature and pressure of their data.
Process heat is the total heat to the reformer train and includes preheat.
Ahn and Lee's heat basis gives a different duty that this model has not reconciled; the dashboard shows the surplus on both bases.
Stage 3 carbon gate. The Level 3 carbon comparison failed, so the gas feed term T13 stays on its anchored value.
The equilibrium layer misses INL's printed conventional reformer conversion.
Input outside its evidence range. Helium supply temperature is fixed at 900 C. Highest measured secondary helium temperature is 859 C, HTTR 2004 high-temperature run (IAEA NP-T-4.3 printed p.14)

wgs.summary: High and low temperature shift beds in one drawn vessel.
lims: No low temperature shift kinetics exist in the local sources; the approach comes from two flowsheets.
One vessel is drawn for two modelled beds.
At Chinchen's test space velocity the high temperature shift misses INL's outlet.
Stage 3 carbon gate. The Level 3 flowsheet gives a different carbon split from the anchored value, and the comparison failed.
The engine's shift heat release row is not run.

syngas_cooler.summary: Heat recovery chain from the reformer exit down to the separator, drawn as one exchanger.
lims: INL Case 5 stands in for Case 6, whose stream sheets are not held locally.
No source gives the heat transfer coefficient or area of these exchangers.
Six exchangers are modelled and one is drawn.

separator.summary: Knock-out drum that removes condensed water before the absorber.
lims: The Headline solve runs no flash; condensate flow comes only from the Level 3 flowsheet.
Condensate chemistry is absent.
CO₂ dissolved in the condensate sits outside the ledger.

absorber.summary: Packed column where 30 wt% MEA takes CO₂ out of the shifted syngas at pressure.
lims: Stage 3 column benchmarks. The pilot absorber benchmark misses, and the high-pressure runs sit far below the measured removal. The column gate failed, so the Headline solve keeps the fixed per-pass capture and the column model runs only in the validation harness.
No pilot has run aqueous MEA on shifted syngas at this pressure.
No solubility data exist in MEA for H₂ or the other light gases, and solvent property data end near the rich loading cap of 0.50 mol/mol.
The liquid to gas ratio is far above that of flue-gas pilots.
The literature on solvent choice is mixed, so Selexol and activated MDEA stay as sensitivities.

lean_pump.summary: Raises lean solvent from stripper pressure to absorber pressure.
lims: Pump and motor efficiencies are project assumptions, and no letdown recovery is credited.
Stage 3 column gate. The column benchmarks failed, so term T07 stays on its anchored value.

lean_cooler.summary: Trims lean solvent to absorber temperature with cooling water.
lims: The cooling electricity factor is an assumption with no direct published ratio.
The anchored port scales the cooling load on the reboiler duty and computes no lean cooler duty.
Stage 3 column gate. The column benchmarks failed, so term T08 stays on its anchored value.

rich_lean_hx.summary: Cross exchanger that heats rich solvent on its way to the stripper with hot lean solvent.
lims: Solvent heat capacity is assumed, since the local data are figures only.
The Headline solve folds this exchanger into the fixed specific reboiler duty and computes no duty for it.

stripper.summary: Regenerates rich MEA near 2.0 bar and releases the captured CO₂ overhead.
lims: Stage 3 column benchmarks. The stripper model misses the pilot regeneration energy and lean loading. The column gate failed, so the Headline solve keeps the approved specific reboiler duty (decision S12 in docs/VALIDATION_MATRIX.md).
No measured specific reboiler duty exists for high-pressure syngas; the value is a judgement carried from flue-gas pilots, and the direction of its bias is unknown.

reboiler.summary: Supplies stripping steam, drawing heat in a fixed order from recovered heat and then reactor steam.
lims: Syngas near the bottom of its recovery range cannot drive this reboiler directly.
All export steam is forfeited at this duty.
The freed Selexol steam credit exists only against INL's flowsheet.
The specific reboiler duty is fixed because the column gate failed.

condenser.summary: Cools the stripper overhead, returns reflux and passes the captured CO₂ on.
lims: H₂ carried into the product CO₂ without a rich flash is a scoping estimate.
The Headline solve folds the condenser into the fixed specific reboiler duty and computes no duty for it.

co2_compressor.summary: Compresses captured CO₂ for the ship and offshore storage.
lims: DICE gives a higher compression load, and the two scopes were not compared.
INL's outlet is a pipeline condition; conditioning for the ship is not modelled.
Stage 3 carbon gate. The Level 3 carbon comparison failed, so term T09 stays on its anchored value.

co2_storage.summary: Ship transport to offshore storage abroad, inside the dashed line as Figure 2 draws it.
lims: Storage is a tariff only, with no simulation.
How offshore storage abroad counts as abatement is unresolved.

psa.summary: Pressure swing adsorption, an external block outside the dashed line.
lims: The PSA is not simulated; recovery is assumed from INL and product purity is INL's.
The reject return is a boundary stream, by project decision.

recycle_compressor.summary: Compresses the PSA reject that crosses back into the boundary for the cryogenic unit.
lims: INL's row covers Case 6 fuel-gas recycle and nitrogen removal equipment together, and the split is not published.
No published cost exists for this train; the ledger line is a proxy.

cryogenic.summary: Returns a CH₄-rich recycle to the reformer feed and H₂ to the PSA feed. The N₂-rich cut goes to the stack.
lims: Stage 3 carbon gate. The Level 3 flowsheet and the anchored ledger disagree on the carbon split after the shift, four carbon lines miss (tube, tail gas, recycled, burned), and term T04 stays on its anchored value.
CO₂ slip into this unit is about ten times INL's, and freeze-out and reverse shift are unquantified, so INL's recycle may not transfer to MEA.
The burned N₂-rich cut leaves to the atmosphere and is counted in the emissions.
